findings.description: TASK-P2-DEV-02 plans TargetKey/ModelPath tests while TASK-P2-DEV-04 is the task that creates the neutral TargetKey/ModelPath/ModelAccessRuleKey and materialization contracts. The declared dependency order lets a compiler slice consume CONTEXT APIs before its provider task is complete and conflicts with compiler -> context dependency direction.
findings.required_change: Make TASK-P2-DEV-04 depend on TASK-P2-DEV-01; make TASK-P2-DEV-02 depend on TASK-P2-DEV-01 and TASK-P2-DEV-04; make TASK-P2-DEV-03 depend on TASK-P2-DEV-02 and TASK-P2-DEV-04; render those tasks in the same topological order.

summary: P1 dependency-order defect: compiler target and policy slices consume CONTEXT neutral APIs before the provider task is complete.

R02 passes scope, vertical-slice, acyclic dependency, exact validation, stop/retry, trace/flow and 23-TestClass coverage checks. R01 dependency-order P1 is corrected by scheduling CONTEXT neutral contracts before compiler consumers.

R02 preserves DESIGN-P2-R30 module direction and trusted boundaries: CONTEXT contracts precede compiler consumers, MODEL precedes STARTER composition, dependency DAG is acyclic, and every development task declares the required wk-ar skeleton/review/advance/concrete/final-review sequence.

R02 maps all 10 stable traces and all 23 TESTDESIGN-P2-R31 exact TestClasses into task validation commands and expected results; each task has blocking test commands and acceptance mapping for success, boundary, denial/failure or integration behavior.

R02 is executable in the current Maven reactor: all five owner modules and wrapper exist, affected-file scopes are bounded, dependency order provides required upstream APIs, every task has exact commands/expected results/stop conditions, and concrete implementation is explicitly blocked by wk-ar first-review/advance gates.
